title: The Art of Strategic Thinking (How to Become Wildly Successful at Anything You Do)

sentences.en: Everyone is racing to be successful right now.
sentences.zh: 现在所有人都在拼命追求成功。

sentences.en: And as you'd guess, 99.99% of them will not, in fact, become successful because they're all obsessed with the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 但你也猜得到，其中 99.99% 的人实际上并不会成功，因为他们全都沉迷于错误的东西。

sentences.en: They're obsessed with the clod code skills that they're collecting from Instagram posts that tell you to comment a keyword in order for them to DMU so you can follow them so that they can send you the link to the skill that you're going to try once and never use again.
sentences.zh: 他们沉迷于那些从 Instagram 帖子里收集来的所谓高收入技能，那些帖子让你评论一个关键词，好让他们能私信你，让你关注他们，然后他们再发给你一个链接，里面是你只会试一次就再也不会用的技能。

sentences.en: They're obsessed with the YouTube videos that teach them how to build a profitable business in five actionable steps, and I still don't understand why people are so obsessed with actionable steps and bullet point summaries, because that's not going to help you in the slightest if you don't have understanding or context or experience.
sentences.zh: 他们沉迷于那些 YouTube 视频，教你怎么用五个可操作步骤建一个赚钱的企业，我至今都不明白为什么人们这么痴迷于可操作步骤和要点总结，因为如果你没有理解、没有背景、没有经验，这些东西对你一点帮助都没有。

sentences.en: They're obsessed with tactics.
sentences.zh: 他们沉迷于战术。

sentences.en: You know, the same knowledge that everyone else has access to.
sentences.zh: 就是那种所有人都能接触到的知识。

sentences.en: Do you not realize that all the information you could ever need to make $100 million is readily available to you online, in books, or just inside of an AI chat if you talk to it long enough.
sentences.zh: 你难道没意识到，你赚一亿美元所需的所有信息，都已经唾手可得地摆在你面前了——在网上、在书里，或者只要你跟 AI 聊得够久，就在聊天框里。

sentences.en: Have you ever stopped and wondered why everyone in the world isn't making millions of dollars right now?
sentences.zh: 你有没有停下来想过，为什么现在不是全世界每个人都在赚几百万美元？

sentences.en: Have you ever considered that the actionable advice you crave so much won't get you anywhere, unless you know how the pieces you're picking up fit into the entire puzzle?
sentences.zh: 你有没有考虑过，你如此渴望的那些可操作建议，根本不会带你走到任何地方，除非你知道你捡起来的这些碎片，该怎么拼进整张拼图里？

sentences.en: So why is this?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Why are so many people trying to desperately aim for success but get nowhere close to achieving it?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么多人拼命瞄准成功，却连边都摸不到？

sentences.en: One is because they're exchanging one form of cheap dopamine for another, more insidious form.
sentences.zh: 第一个原因是，他们在用一种廉价的快感，去交换另一种更隐蔽的快感。

sentences.en: I would argue that endless tactic collection by endlessly consuming YouTube videos around business and self-improvement is worse than just doom scrolling brain rot videos, because you're getting a sense of fake progress.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，通过无休止地刷商业和自我提升类 YouTube 视频来无休止地收集战术，比单纯刷那些让人变蠢的垃圾视频更糟糕，因为你获得了一种虚假的进步感。

sentences.en: At least with the doom scrolling videos, you just feel bad about yourself.
sentences.zh: 刷垃圾视频，你至少只是觉得自己很糟糕。

sentences.en: But with the self-improvement in business and even this video, you feel bad about yourself.
sentences.zh: 但刷自我提升和商业类视频，包括你现在看的这个，你也会觉得自己很糟糕。

sentences.en: But you also get this false certainty that you're making progress just by watching the video.
sentences.zh: 但同时你还会获得一种虚假的确定感，觉得光是看了这个视频，自己就在进步了。

sentences.en: The second reason is because they don't have a strategy that allows them to use the tactics they're collecting to their highest degree tactic, collection or tactics in general, which is just execution strategy is positioning.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因是，他们没有一套战略，能让他们把收集到的战术发挥到最大效用。战术收集，或者说战术本身，只是执行。战略是定位。

sentences.en: Tactics is execution.
sentences.zh: 战术是执行。

sentences.en: If you don't have a strategy, that one exposes you to the right tactics that you didn't even know about in the first place, or didn't register as an opportunity, then you're just going to be thrown around like a puppet by internet marketers because they know how to capture your attention and persuade you that something is valuable, even if it may not fit your specific situation and your specific mind.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有战略——一套能让你接触到正确战术的战略，那些你一开始根本不知道、或者根本没意识到是机会的战术——那你就会像木偶一样被网络营销师们随意摆布，因为他们知道怎么抓住你的注意力，说服你某样东西很有价值，即使它可能根本不适合你的具体情况和你的特定思维。

sentences.en: Now, if you're this type of person who just collects tactics, I'm not trying to belittle you.
sentences.zh: 如果你就是这种只收集战术的人，我不是在贬低你。

sentences.en: I do the same thing quite often right now, and I did it a lot more in the past.
sentences.zh: 我现在也经常做同样的事，过去做得更多。

sentences.en: I got stuck into hell.
sentences.zh: 我曾经深陷地狱。

sentences.en: I took all the courses I tried and failed at seven different business models Facebook ads, SEO, dropshipping, web design, digital art, and a few more.
sentences.zh: 我上了所有课程，尝试并失败了七种不同的商业模式：Facebook 广告、SEO、一件代发、网页设计、数字艺术，还有几个别的。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't even consider them businesses.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都不认为那些是生意。

sentences.en: I would consider them hobbies because I would learn the high value skill and that felt good.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们是爱好，因为我会去学那个高价值技能，那感觉很好。

sentences.en: I would start the LLC and that felt good.
sentences.zh: 我会去注册公司，那感觉很好。

sentences.en: I would build the website and try to write the copy for it so that it's persuasive, and that felt good.
sentences.zh: 我会去建网站，试着写有说服力的文案，那感觉很好。

sentences.en: But when it came to actually getting a customer, getting someone to pay me, I was nowhere to be found.
sentences.zh: 但到了真正要获取客户、让别人付钱给我的时候，我就消失得无影无踪了。

sentences.en: And the missing piece was a strategy, but not just a strategy, the ability to think strategically because how else are you going to create a strategy?
sentences.zh: 缺失的那一环是战略，但不仅仅是战略，而是战略思考的能力，因为不然你怎么可能创造出战略？

sentences.en: And that's an incredibly difficult thing to learn.
sentences.zh: 而这是一件极其难学的事。

sentences.en: But that's what we're here to talk about.
sentences.zh: 但这正是我们今天要谈的。

sentences.en: That's the secret behind Steve Jobs, Alexander the great military strategist in general, most great and successful people that we look up to have the ability to think strategically.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Steve Jobs、亚历山大大帝、所有军事战略家，以及大多数我们仰望的伟大成功人士背后的秘密：他们都具备战略思考的能力。

sentences.en: They may not say that that is their superpower or their secret because they may be unconsciously competent, but that is exactly it.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不会说这是他们的超能力或秘密，因为他们可能已经无意识地精通了，但事实就是如此。

sentences.en: It all comes down to strategy.
sentences.zh: 一切都归结于战略。

sentences.en: And that's what I'm going to show you, not only how to learn, but how to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我要展示给你的，不只是怎么学，更是怎么做。

sentences.en: In this video, we're going to create a life strategy, and you're going to learn the principles that you can take and apply to anything that you do, be it business, sports, relationships, anything.
sentences.zh: 在这个视频里，我们要制定一套人生战略，你会学到一些原则，可以拿去用在任何事上——商业、体育、人际关系，什么都行。

sentences.en: We're also going to talk about the nine traits of a master strategist, and especially how a lack of strategy means a lack of control over the outcome of your life.
sentences.zh: 我们还会聊到顶级战略家的九个特质，尤其是：缺乏战略，就意味着你对人生的结果缺乏掌控。

sentences.en: As we begin, the only thing I ask of you is that you actually listen and attempt to implement what I say.
sentences.zh: 开始之前，我对你只有一个要求：认真听，并且试着把我说的东西落地执行。

sentences.en: You take notes, you actually do something.
sentences.zh: 做笔记，真正去做点什么。

sentences.en: Aside from just watching the video and then letting it leave your mind 30 minutes later.
sentences.zh: 而不是看完视频，三十分钟后就忘得一干二净。

sentences.en: So section number one strategy is getting yourself into a superior position, while at the same time making sure your opponent is in a worse one.
sentences.zh: 第一节：战略，就是让自己占据优势位置，同时确保对手处于劣势。

sentences.en: In this section is all about understanding the quote.
sentences.zh: 这一节的核心，就是理解这句话。

sentences.en: Tactics flow from a superior position from Bobby Fischer, who is a chess grandmaster.
sentences.zh: “战术从优势位置中自然流出。”——Bobby Fischer，国际象棋特级大师。

sentences.en: Now let's walk through a simple chess match.
sentences.zh: 我们来快速过一局棋。

sentences.en: I'll try not to bore you here.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不让你觉得无聊。

sentences.en: We'll make it quick just so we can get to the point.
sentences.zh: 快速讲完，直击要点。

sentences.en: But player one in the chess match spends the first part of the game doing things that look boring.
sentences.zh: 棋局中，玩家一在开局阶段做的那些事，看起来很无聊。

sentences.en: They aren't attacking, they aren't capturing any pieces.
sentences.zh: 他们没有进攻，也没有吃子。

sentences.en: And from the outside, it looks like they're not doing anything.
sentences.zh: 从外面看，好像什么都没干。

sentences.en: They're just moving their pieces to certain squares on the board.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把棋子挪到棋盘上的某些格子。

sentences.en: And in a game like chess, you're playing on a grid, but not all of the squares on that grid are created equal.
sentences.zh: 在国际象棋里，你是在一个格子上对弈，但不是所有格子都生来平等。

sentences.en: It's the same with life.
sentences.zh: 人生也一样。

sentences.en: A piece in the center of a board can reach many more places than a piece stuck behind a corner.
sentences.zh: 一颗在棋盘中央的棋子，能触及的位置远比一颗困在角落里的棋子多得多。

sentences.en: Now in the game, player one slides a rook onto an open lane where nothing blocks it.
sentences.zh: 棋局中，玩家一把车滑到一条畅通无阻的开放线路上。

sentences.en: They place a bishop on a path that points straight at the enemy king.
sentences.zh: 他们把象放在一条直指对方王的路径上。

sentences.en: They place a knight on a square near the middle of the board, and meanwhile player two has pieces just getting in each other's way.
sentences.zh: 他们把马放在靠近棋盘中央的格子，而与此同时，玩家二的棋子却在互相挡路。

sentences.en: Their most powerful pieces are trapped behind their own pawns.
sentences.zh: 他们最强大的棋子被自己的兵困在后面。

sentences.en: Their king is stuck in the middle of the board because they never found a safe moment to tuck it away in a corner.
sentences.zh: 他们的王卡在棋盘中央，因为他们始终没找到安全时机把它藏到角落去。

sentences.en: Player two was only reacting to player one's moves, so player one moves their knight to a square where it can attack player two's king and queen at the same time, and in chess this is called a fork, so your opponent can only save one.
sentences.zh: 玩家二只是在被动应对玩家一的每一步，于是玩家一把马跳到一个能同时攻击玩家二的王和后的格子，这在象棋里叫“捉双”——对手只能救一个。

sentences.en: Those are two very powerful pieces, the king and the queen, so losing either one is not good.
sentences.zh: 那是两颗非常强大的棋子，王和后，丢掉哪一个都不好。

sentences.en: So of course player two has to move his king so he doesn't lose the game.
sentences.zh: 所以玩家二当然得挪王，不然就输棋了。

sentences.en: But that leads to player one being able to take their queen, which is the most powerful piece on the board.
sentences.zh: 但这导致玩家一能吃掉了他们的后，那是棋盘上最强大的棋子。

sentences.en: And it's essentially game over at this point.
sentences.zh: 到这一步，棋局基本结束了。

sentences.en: But the thing here is, the lesson is that any player who got to that exact arrangement of pieces could have played that game winning move.
sentences.zh: 但这里的关键是，教训在于：任何一个能走到那个精确棋子布局的玩家，都能打出那步制胜棋。

sentences.en: The reason player one got there is because they spent the entire game building up to it.
sentences.zh: 玩家一之所以能走到那里，是因为他们整局棋都在为这一刻铺路。

sentences.en: So if you were to remove any of those boring steps from the start, the fork or the game winning tactic wouldn't exist.
sentences.zh: 如果你把开局那些看似无聊的步骤拿掉任何一步，那个“捉双”或者制胜战术就不会存在。

sentences.en: The knight would have gotten blocked and the king would have escaped as the defending piece arrived.
sentences.zh: 马会被挡住，王会在防守棋子赶到时逃脱。

sentences.en: So the real lesson is strategy is getting yourself into a superior position, while at the same time making sure your opponent is in a worse one.
sentences.zh: 所以真正的教训是：战略，就是让自己占据优势位置，同时确保对手处于劣势。

sentences.en: Strategy is the work of making your position better and your opponent's position worse.
sentences.zh: 战略就是不断优化自己的位置，同时削弱对手的位置。

sentences.en: Move by move into the gap between the two is so large that tactics start appearing on their own.
sentences.zh: 一步一步来，当双方差距大到一定程度，战术就会自然浮现。

sentences.en: Now, the interesting thing here is that in the game of life, you are both the opponent and the player.
sentences.zh: 有意思的是，在人生这场游戏里，你既是玩家，也是对手。

sentences.en: Every decision you make changes your own position, and most people are just completely blind to where they are.
sentences.zh: 你的每一个决定都在改变自己的位置，而大多数人对自己身在何处完全无知。

sentences.en: If the average person's life were a chess match, they probably have gotten into a game winning move before, but they didn't even realize it.
sentences.zh: 如果把普通人的一生比作一盘棋，他们很可能早就走到过一招制胜的关键点，但自己根本没意识到。

sentences.en: They weren't able to act on that opportunity because it was just unconscious to them.
sentences.zh: 他们无法抓住那个机会，因为那对他们来说完全是无意识的。

sentences.en: They didn't have the cognitive flexibility or architecture, which we're going to talk about in the next video, to actually know when they can execute on a specific tactic to get a big reward.
sentences.zh: 他们缺乏认知的灵活性或架构——这个我们下期视频会讲——去真正判断什么时候该执行某个具体战术来获取巨大回报。

sentences.en: That's why strategy has to come first, because if you want to actually succeed at building the side business or the creator business, like we talk about here, or just building an esthetic physique, or becoming healthy or simply getting what you want out of life.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么战略必须先行。如果你想真正做成点什么，无论是打造副业、创作者事业——就像我们这里聊的——还是练出好看的身材、变得健康，或者干脆从人生中得到你想要的。

sentences.en: You can't be like most people because most people spend zero time strategizing.
sentences.zh: 你就不能像大多数人一样，因为大多数人花在战略思考上的时间是零。

sentences.en: They don't engage in intentional strategic thinking like, think about your own life, right?
sentences.zh: 他们从不进行有意识的战略思考。想想你自己的人生，对吧？

sentences.en: I do this all the time. We all do.
sentences.zh: 我经常做这件事。我们都一样。

sentences.en: But when you're just going about your life, are you actually thinking, or are you just reacting to thoughts and emotions?
sentences.zh: 但当你日复一日地生活时，你是在真正思考，还是只是在对外界的念头和情绪做出反应？

sentences.en: Are you understanding what's going on in your head or are you just letting it play out?
sentences.zh: 你是在理解自己脑子里发生了什么，还是任由它自动播放？

sentences.en: Both have their benefits, right?
sentences.zh: 两种方式各有好处，对吧？

sentences.en: They're different modes of thinking.
sentences.zh: 它们是不同的思维模式。

sentences.en: There's creativity and there's productivity.
sentences.zh: 一种是创造力，一种是生产力。

sentences.en: Creativity benefits from a more open focus, letting your mind be kind of chaotic and then picking, picking certain ideas or pieces and synthesizing them together.
sentences.zh: 创造力受益于更开放的注意力，让你的思绪保持一种混沌状态，然后从中挑选某些想法或片段，把它们合成起来。

sentences.en: And then productivity is more strategic, more focused, more hierarchical.
sentences.zh: 而生产力则更具战略性、更聚焦、更有层级。

sentences.en: But most people don't engage in productivity in that way.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人并不是以这种方式进行生产的。

sentences.en: They engage in a very narrow state of stressful focus based on urgency or scarcity, because they have to to survive, and that is not a good place to be in.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入一种非常狭隘的、基于紧迫感或匮乏感的压力性专注，因为他们必须这样才能生存，而这绝不是一个好的处境。

sentences.en: And lastly, if you observe society, you will see that plain tactic level thinking is very disastrous.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你观察社会，你会发现纯粹的战术层面思考是灾难性的。

sentences.en: And that leads into section number two, which is that the average person lives in a mindless cycle of struggles they can't escape.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第二部分：普通人活在一个他们无法逃脱的、无意识的挣扎循环里。

sentences.en: So thank goodness you aren't actually on a battlefield because you'd probably be dead.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢天谢地你不是真的在战场上，否则你可能早就没命了。

sentences.en: Most people commit highly predictable strategic mistakes that if they were in a truly violent setting, they would lose and winners would be studying what they did so that they could do the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 大多数人会犯下高度可预测的战略错误，如果放在真正残酷的环境里，他们早就输了，而赢家会研究他们的做法，然后反着来。

sentences.en: Getting married too early or late, not developing mastery in anything, trusting that AI can do everything for you.
sentences.zh: 过早或过晚结婚，不在任何事情上深耕精通，盲目相信 AI 能替你搞定一切。

sentences.en: And I'm saying this as someone who is not anti-air completely, because everything is a religion nowadays and we don't have to treat anti-air or the flavor of the day drama that's going on, that's been happening every three months is just a different thing that people get obsessed with and cry about and play victim with.
sentences.zh: 我说这话，并不是说我完全反 AI，因为现在什么都搞得跟宗教似的，我们没必要去站队反 AI 或者掺和那些隔三差五就冒出来的热门闹剧，每三个月就换个花样，人们沉迷其中、哭天喊地、扮演受害者。

sentences.en: In virtue signal on social media.
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体上搞道德表演。

sentences.en: You don't have to engage in that, and you can see the signs of lower levels of thinking in those people, and you can avoid them.
sentences.zh: 你不需要参与那些，你可以从那些人身上看到低层次思维的迹象，然后避开他们。

sentences.en: Again, we're going to talk about that in the next video.
sentences.zh: 同样，这个我们下期视频再聊。

sentences.en: But other examples chasing money over meaning irresponsibly, going into debt, staying in a bad relationship, not investing in education, climbing a corporate ladder that leads to nowhere.
sentences.zh: 其他例子还有：不负责任地追逐金钱而非意义、背上债务、困在一段糟糕的关系里、不投资教育、爬一条哪也到不了的职场阶梯。

sentences.en: The list just goes on.
sentences.zh: 这个清单可以一直列下去。

sentences.en: The average person does not try to solve their problems or their struggles.
sentences.zh: 普通人并不试图解决自己的问题或挣扎。

sentences.en: They get stuck in a routine where they live the same day over and over again, because that's what the conditioning process led to in their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入了一种日复一日重复同一天的日常，因为这就是他们人生中被规训出来的结果。

sentences.en: When they were born, their parents and teachers injected values and beliefs into their head that put them on the default path, heading toward the goal that society wanted for them, which is go to school, get a job, retire at 65.
sentences.zh: 从出生起，父母和老师就把价值观和信念注入他们的大脑，把他们推上默认路径，走向社会为他们设定的目标：上学、找工作、65岁退休。

sentences.en: The industrial paradigm.
sentences.zh: 工业范式。

sentences.en: And most people never question that.
sentences.zh: 大多数人从未质疑过这一点。

sentences.en: And by the time they turned 20, it had become so conditioned in their mind that it's just habitual, it's just unconscious.
sentences.zh: 到他们20岁时，这已经深深印在脑子里，变成了习惯，变成了无意识行为。

sentences.en: It's just what they do.
sentences.zh: 变成了他们理所当然会做的事。

sentences.en: It doesn't cross their minds to snap out of it, engage in strategic thinking, and change the direction of their life so that they can eventually reach a more advantageous position.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不会想到要跳出来，进行战略思考，改变人生方向，最终到达一个更有利的位置。

sentences.en: Where their problems aren't so painful, they still have problems.
sentences.zh: 在那个位置上，他们的问题不会那么痛苦——问题依然存在。

sentences.en: Everyone still has problems, but they're of a lesser magnitude.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有问题，但问题的量级会小很多。

sentences.en: They're more fun and creative problems to solve.
sentences.zh: 那些问题更有趣、更有创造性。

sentences.en: You start to see life as a puzzle rather than a death sentence.
sentences.zh: 你开始把人生看作一个谜题，而不是死刑判决。

sentences.en: So what I'm saying is that everyone has a strategy, but for most people, it's not one that they created, it's one that they were assigned.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说的是，每个人都有策略，但对大多数人来说，那不是他们自己创造的，而是被分配的。

sentences.en: Their strategy is again, go to school, get a job, retire at 65, be a good student, make a decent amount of money even though it's not that much.
sentences.zh: 他们的策略还是那一套：上学、找工作、65岁退休、做个好学生、赚一份还算体面的钱——虽然也没多少。

sentences.en: Be humble.
sentences.zh: 要谦虚。

sentences.en: Don't stick your nose out.
sentences.zh: 别出头。

sentences.en: Your dreams aren't worth pursuing because they're risky.
sentences.zh: 你的梦想不值得追求，因为太冒险。

sentences.en: Which doesn't make sense because risk is the only way to get reward.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通，因为风险是获得回报的唯一途径。

sentences.en: It all just doesn't make sense when you actually think about it.
sentences.zh: 当你真正去思考的时候，这一切都说不通。

sentences.en: Especially going into the new paradigm, which is AI information, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 尤其是进入新范式之后——AI、信息，所有这些。

sentences.en: It requires a completely different strategy, whether or not you agree that culture and society should be heading in this direction of AI and information, that doesn't mean that it's not happening.
sentences.zh: 这需要一套完全不同的策略。不管你是否认同文化和社会应该朝着AI和信息这个方向走，都不意味着它没有在发生。

sentences.en: People are so mad that, oh, jobs are going to be replaced, even though I don't know if that's going to be the case.
sentences.zh: 人们很愤怒，说工作会被取代——虽然我不确定会不会真的如此。

sentences.en: But that's what people are saying.
sentences.zh: 但人们就是这么说的。

sentences.en: No matter what it is, you need to create a new strategy so that you can thrive in the future, rather than being stuck in the one that you were assigned.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，你需要创造一套新策略，让自己在未来蓬勃发展，而不是困在被分配的那一套里。

sentences.en: That was only somewhat beneficial to the old way of life, the American dream.
sentences.zh: 那一套只对旧的生活方式、对美国梦还算有点用。

sentences.en: So how do you actually start to get out of this mindless and honestly meaningless way of living?
sentences.zh: 那么，你该如何真正开始摆脱这种无意识、说实话也毫无意义的生活方式？

sentences.en: And you may not be completely in it, but this still applies to you to start to create your own strategy.
sentences.zh: 你可能没有完全陷进去，但这依然适用于你——开始创造你自己的策略。

sentences.en: Well, you think of it as if you're on an actual battlefield, because in many ways you are.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成你正身处真实的战场，因为在很多方面，你确实如此。

sentences.en: You're living under this guy's of modern comfort and convenience, where everything is just easy and you're allowed to just coast through life and do the bare minimum in order to survive.
sentences.zh: 你生活在这个现代舒适与便利的伪装之下，一切都太容易了，你可以就这么混一辈子，只做最低限度的事来维持生存。

sentences.en: But if you were on a battlefield, think of the general.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在战场上，想想那位将军。

sentences.en: His own life was on the line that forced strategic depth.
sentences.zh: 他自己的命悬一线，这迫使他必须有战略深度。

sentences.en: He had to be strategic in order to win or else he would die.
sentences.zh: 他必须讲战略才能赢，否则就会死。

sentences.en: You need pressure.
sentences.zh: 你需要压力。

sentences.en: You need tactical stress.
sentences.zh: 你需要战术性压力。

sentences.en: You need to put yourself in a position where you must craft a strategy or you lose, or else you're just going to lose.
sentences.zh: 你需要把自己放在一个位置上，让你必须制定策略，否则就输——否则你就是会输。

sentences.en: Either way, move into an apartment you can't afford.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，搬进一间你负担不起的公寓。

sentences.en: Book the plane ticket to somewhere you've never been.
sentences.zh: 订一张去你从未去过的地方的机票。

sentences.en: Invest in the business, software, the course, or coaching.
sentences.zh: 投资那个生意、软件、课程或教练服务。

sentences.en: Even if you think it's a scam, because at least your finances will be put on the line and you can't live in a shroud of false comfort anymore.
sentences.zh: 哪怕你觉得它是骗局，至少你的钱被押上去了，你再也无法活在虚假的舒适里。

sentences.en: So you get it.
sentences.zh: 所以你懂了。

sentences.en: You need a strategy, and you need to develop the skill of strategic thinking.
sentences.zh: 你需要一套战略，你需要培养战略思维这项技能。

sentences.en: Because without those, every single decision you make in life becomes arbitrary.
sentences.zh: 因为没有这些，你人生中做的每一个决定都会变得随意。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 无所谓。

sentences.en: It is quite literally meaningless because it's not aimed in a specific direction.
sentences.zh: 它几乎毫无意义，因为它没有瞄准一个明确的方向。

sentences.en: That doesn't feel good to think about that.
sentences.zh: 想到这个感觉并不好。

sentences.en: Every single thing that you do every single day without a strategy does not get you anywhere.
sentences.zh: 没有战略，你每天做的每一件事都不会把你带到任何地方。

sentences.en: I'm being hyperbolic, but that's for a reason to actually get you to take this seriously.
sentences.zh: 我是在夸张，但这是有原因的，就是为了让你真正认真对待这件事。

sentences.en: And if the outcome of your life is the accumulation of the decisions you make, then this is arguably one of the most important things you could ever do.
sentences.zh: 如果你人生的结果是所有决定的累积，那这可以说是你能做的最重要的事之一。

sentences.en: That leads to section number three how to build a superior life position.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第三部分：如何构建一个优势人生位置。

sentences.en: By going so deep, you see patterns in everything you do.
sentences.zh: 通过钻得足够深，让你在所做的一切中看到模式。

sentences.en: Now.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: In the Book of Five Rings by Miyamoto Musashi, there are nine precepts or principles every strategist should follow.
sentences.zh: 在宫本武藏的《五轮书》中，有九条每个战略家都应遵循的训诫或原则。

sentences.en: One is don't think dishonestly.
sentences.zh: 一是不要不诚实地思考。

sentences.en: Two training is the way itself.
sentences.zh: 二是训练本身就是道。

sentences.en: Three get acquainted with every art, for know the ways of all professions.
sentences.zh: 三是通晓诸艺，了解所有职业的门道。

sentences.en: Five understand gain and loss in worldly dealings six develop intuitive judgment about everything.
sentences.zh: 五是懂得世间事务中的得失，六是对一切事物培养直觉判断。

sentences.en: Seven perceive what can't be seen eight.
sentences.zh: 七是感知不可见之物，八是。

sentences.en: Attend even two small things nine.
sentences.zh: 连小事也要留心，九是。

sentences.en: Do nothing useless.
sentences.zh: 不做无用之事。

sentences.en: A strategist in Musashi's mind is someone who goes so deep into one discipline that they discover something universal.
sentences.zh: 在武藏看来，战略家是那种在一个领域钻得极深、以至于发现了某种普适真理的人。

sentences.en: At the bottom of it, you notice patterns that aren't specific to business or relationships or swordsmanship or chess.
sentences.zh: 在它的底部，你会注意到那些并非商业、人际关系、剑术或棋局所特有的模式。

sentences.en: They are constants.
sentences.zh: 它们是恒常不变的。

sentences.en: And once you see those patterns and notice them across domains, you become far more effective within all domains because you are never really starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 一旦你看到这些模式，并在不同领域间注意到它们，你在所有领域都会变得高效得多，因为你从来都不是真正从零开始。

sentences.en: You have an understanding of reality as a whole on your side.
sentences.zh: 你拥有对现实整体的理解作为后盾。

sentences.en: We'll go into how to uncover these like universal patterns, so to say.
sentences.zh: 我们会深入探讨如何发现这些所谓的普适模式。

sentences.en: But the first time I became aware of this is when I started in business, because for most of my life, I had been into fitness and in the gym and studying nutrition and all of this stuff just in my free time.
sentences.zh: 但我第一次意识到这一点，是在我开始创业的时候，因为我人生大部分时间都沉迷于健身、泡在健身房、研究营养学，全是空闲时间做的事。

sentences.en: And when I started building the business and actually seeing some success with it, I'm like, this is progressive overload, right?
sentences.zh: 当我开始建立事业并真正看到一些成果时，我心想，这不就是渐进超负荷吗？

sentences.en: If you know what progressive overload is, where it's like slowly increasing the weight over time, you're not trying to jump up in huge leaps and bounds of weight.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道渐进超负荷是什么，就是随着时间慢慢增加重量，而不是试图一下子猛跳上去。

sentences.en: You increase by 2.5 pounds or 5 pounds, and the nutrition you eat has to fuel the recovery to facilitate that.
sentences.zh: 你每次增加2.5磅或5磅，而你摄入的营养必须为恢复提供燃料，来促成这个过程。

sentences.en: And you use that as a metric for how much you're growing, because if you can focus on that, that is a great proxy for muscle growth, for understanding how much muscle you're actually building and whether or not you're building muscle is if you're consistently getting stronger over time.
sentences.zh: 你把它当作衡量自己成长程度的指标，因为如果你能专注于它，它就是肌肉增长的一个绝佳代理指标，用来理解你到底长了多少肌肉，以及你是否在长肌肉，就看你是不是在持续地变得更强。

sentences.en: So all of the variables have to come together in order to build muscle, which is the end result.
sentences.zh: 所以所有变量必须协同作用，才能达成肌肉增长这个最终结果。

sentences.en: But in business, making money, the same exact thing happens.
sentences.zh: 但在商业和赚钱上，完全一样的事情也在发生。

sentences.en: You need all of the variables to come together, and you're not aiming for a viral explosion of sales like many of the startups are, you're aiming for the slow, consistent growth, and year after year you look back and you're like,
sentences.zh: 你需要所有变量汇聚到一起，而且你追求的不是像很多创业公司那样销量病毒式爆发，你追求的是缓慢、持续的增长，年复一年你回头看，你会觉得，

sentences.en: Holy crap, this has been an exponential line.
sentences.zh: 天啊，这竟然是一条指数曲线。

sentences.en: Now the nine precepts or principles that we went over define what this strategist or master strategist looks like on the outside.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才讲过的这九条准则或原则，定义了这位战略家或战略大师的外在是什么样子。

sentences.en: So the modern idea of a generalist is usually someone who knows a little about a lot.
sentences.zh: 现代对通才的理解，通常是一个什么都知道一点的人。

sentences.en: There are jack of all trades, but what Musashi is describing here is a bit different.
sentences.zh: 他们是万金油，但武藏在这里描述的东西有点不同。

sentences.en: There's the generalist, there's the specialist, and then there's the master or the strategist.
sentences.zh: 有通才，有专才，然后还有大师或战略家。

sentences.en: And this also maps quite well to the stages of ego development and Spiral Dynamics.
sentences.zh: 这也很贴合自我发展层次理论和螺旋动力学的各个阶段。

sentences.en: The strategist stage is quite achievable and comes with the following qualities.
sentences.zh: 战略家阶段是完全可以达到的，并且具备以下特质。

sentences.en: The first is systems thinking.
sentences.zh: 第一是系统思维。

sentences.en: So strategists see competing systems and perspective simultaneously, while achievers who are the self-help or the businessman operate within a single system of success and achievement.
sentences.zh: 战略家能同时看到相互竞争的系统与视角，而成就者，也就是那些搞自我提升或做生意的人，只在单一的成功与成就系统内运作。

sentences.en: They're also comfortable with paradox, so they can hold contradictions like being both pro and anti-air, rather than resolving them into clear or false answers.
sentences.zh: 他们也对悖论感到自在，所以能容纳矛盾，比如同时支持和不支持 AI，而不是把它们归结为清晰或错误的答案。

sentences.en: They focus on process over outcome, so they care about how things happen and the principles at play, not just the results.
sentences.zh: 他们关注过程而非结果，所以他们在乎事情如何发生以及背后的原则，而不仅仅是结果。

sentences.en: They're aware of constraints, so they see how their assumptions and frameworks shape what they perceive.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到约束的存在，所以能看到自己的假设和框架如何塑造了他们所感知到的东西。

sentences.en: They have a sense of meta awareness, so strategists can observe their own meaning making and not just deploy expertise or navigate social dynamics.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种元意识，所以战略家能观察自己创造意义的过程，而不仅仅是施展专业技能或驾驭社交动态。

sentences.en: And they have principled flexibility.
sentences.zh: 他们还有原则性的灵活。

sentences.en: They have strong values, but adapt methods fluidly versus rigid rules or social conformity.
sentences.zh: 他们有强大的价值观，但会根据情况灵活调整方法，而不是固守僵化的规则或随大流。

sentences.en: The most important trait there, in my opinion, is the ability to hold paradox or to hold multiple frameworks or perspectives.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，那里最重要的特质，是容纳悖论或容纳多种框架和视角的能力。

sentences.en: What that means is not engaging in black and white thinking, which is the lowest form of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 这意味着不陷入非黑即白的思维，那是智力最低级的形式。

sentences.en: And this is one massive trap of social media.
sentences.zh: 这是社交媒体的一个巨大陷阱。

sentences.en: Every time you log on, that's all you see and you react to it and you get addicted to it without even knowing it, and you slowly degrade your mental capacity to hold paradox.
sentences.zh: 每次你登录，你看到的全是这些，你对它们做出反应，在不知不觉中上瘾，然后你容纳悖论的心智能力就慢慢退化了。

sentences.en: So as a side note, the solution to that is to become a curator, you need to carefully protect your mind and curate your own sources of information where you're getting information from.
sentences.zh: 所以顺便提一句，解决方法是成为一个策展人，你需要小心保护你的头脑，精心策展你自己的信息来源，也就是你获取信息的地方。

sentences.en: This is why we built the reader and idea capture inside of Eden.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在 Eden 里构建阅读器和灵感捕捉功能的原因。

sentences.en: You can save a link to anything like this YouTube video, and then open it in a reader so you can highlight it and keep your curated information in one place, organized on boards.
sentences.zh: 你可以保存任何东西的链接，比如这个 YouTube 视频，然后在阅读器里打开它，这样你就可以高亮它，把你精心策展的信息保存在一个地方，用看板组织起来。

sentences.en: And for people who are creators who actually use social media for research, we have a discover feed which shows you the top performing posts, so then you can save those to boards, reverse engineer them, study them, and then use them as inspiration to synthesize into your own writing or work, or YouTube scripts or newsletters or social posts.
sentences.zh: 对于那些真正用社交媒体做研究的创作者，我们有一个发现信息流，会展示表现最好的帖子，然后你可以把它们保存到看板，逆向拆解它们，研究它们，然后用它们作为灵感，融合到你自己的写作或工作中，或者 YouTube 脚本、newsletter 或社交媒体帖子中。

sentences.en: So if you want to start building your garden for ideas, you can start with Eden.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想开始构建你的灵感花园，可以从 Eden 开始。

sentences.en: The idea capture portion and reading is free via the link in the description.
sentences.zh: 灵感捕捉和阅读部分是免费的，链接在描述区。

sentences.en: Strategists see their own constructions as choices their identity, their values, their worldview.
sentences.zh: 战略家把自己构建的东西看作选择，他们的身份、价值观、世界观。

sentences.en: The master or strategist receives the benefits of both the generalist and the specialist, both the ability to be good at many things so they don't narrow their mind to one area of study, limiting their potential and the ability to excel significantly at one thing so they can get outsized results, preferably in a meaningful domain.
sentences.zh: 大师或战略家同时获得通才和专才的好处，既有擅长很多事情的能力，这样他们就不会把思维局限在一个研究领域，限制自己的潜力，又有在一件事情上极其出色的能力，这样他们能获得超常的结果，最好是在一个有意义的领域。

sentences.en: So that is our goal to become someone who can embody these precepts or principles of the strategist.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的目标，就是成为能够体现这些战略家准则或原则的人。

sentences.en: And closer to the end, I'll actually give you a shortcut or as close to a shortcut as you can get to just studying these universal principles directly so that you can notice them in your life.
sentences.zh: 在接近结尾的地方，我会给你一条捷径，或者说尽可能接近捷径的东西，就是直接学习这些普适原则，这样你就能在生活中注意到它们。

sentences.en: And for this section, I think the most actionable point is the ninth precept, which is to do nothing useless.
sentences.zh: 对于这一部分，我认为最具行动力的一点是第九条准则：不做无用之事。

sentences.en: Make that your operating principle for the next year and you will do incredible things.
sentences.zh: 让它成为你接下来一年的行动原则，你会做出了不起的事情。

sentences.en: If you were to simply audit your thoughts and behavior for usefulness, you would rapidly turn your life around.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是去审视自己的思想和行为是否有用，你就能迅速扭转你的人生。

sentences.en: As I said, scrolling on social media, getting sucked in to the dogmatic black and white thinking is useless.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，刷社交媒体、被那些非黑即白的教条思维裹挟，毫无用处。

sentences.en: The mindless way of life is a useless way of life.
sentences.zh: 无意识的生活方式，就是一种无用的生活方式。

sentences.en: So the questions now are what do you actually master?
sentences.zh: 所以现在的问题是，你到底要精通什么？

sentences.en: What is your form of training?
sentences.zh: 你的训练形式是什么？

sentences.en: How do you begin to understand gain and loss?
sentences.zh: 你如何开始理解得与失？

sentences.en: How do you begin to embody the principles of a master strategist?
sentences.zh: 你如何开始内化一个战略大师的原则？

sentences.en: And most importantly in my eyes, how do you do something useful that leads to section four, which is how to think?
sentences.zh: 而在我眼里最重要的是，你如何做一些有用的事，从而导向第四部分——如何思考？

sentences.en: So strategically, you finally take back control of your life.
sentences.zh: 这样，从战略层面，你终于夺回了人生的掌控权。

sentences.en: So thankfully we can study what makes a good strategy or what strategic thinking looks like, and then we can reverse engineer it, take the principles and start to apply them to our life.
sentences.zh: 好在我们可以研究什么构成一个好战略，或者说战略思维长什么样，然后反推它，提取原则，开始应用到我们的人生中。

sentences.en: And these principles have been refined and iterated on over centuries of military and war and sports and business.
sentences.zh: 这些原则经过了几百年军事、战争、体育和商业的打磨和迭代。

sentences.en: You have a massive amount of historical wins and losses that you can look at.
sentences.zh: 你有海量的历史胜败案例可以参考。

sentences.en: And the beautiful thing is that all of these apply to your own personal life and success.
sentences.zh: 而美妙之处在于，这一切都适用于你个人的生活和成功。

sentences.en: I've personally compiled seven of them here, so if you sit down and actually do this and follow through with this, your life will change.
sentences.zh: 我个人整理了其中七条，如果你坐下来真正去做、去执行到底，你的人生会改变。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that your strategy is going to be a winning strategy.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你的战略一定会是赢的战略。

sentences.en: You can still lose, but it sure helps you in not being trampled over by your opponent, which is often yourself.
sentences.zh: 你依然可能输，但它绝对能帮你避免被对手碾压，而那个对手往往就是你自己。

sentences.en: So principle one of strategic thinking is vision.
sentences.zh: 所以战略思维的第一条原则是愿景。

sentences.en: And I love this quote from the account Orange Book on X. No one ever suddenly gets lucky.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢 X 上 Orange Book 这个账号的一句话：没有人是突然走运的。

sentences.en: If the star is suddenly aligned for you, you actually align them, consciously or not, by choosing where to live, who to learn from, who to marry, who to befriend, what lifestyle to maintain, what risks to take, and what vision to believe in.
sentences.zh: 如果星辰突然为你排列整齐，那其实是你自己排列的，无论有意还是无意——通过选择住在哪里、向谁学习、和谁结婚、和谁交朋友、维持什么生活方式、承担什么风险、相信什么愿景。

sentences.en: Now, if you don't have a vision, you're lost.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有愿景，你就是迷失的。

sentences.en: You do not have intention behind your actions because you don't know what your actions are leading to.
sentences.zh: 你的行动背后没有意图，因为你不知道你的行动在导向什么。

sentences.en: You're holding ten darts in your hand, and those represent the ten bold decisions that will determine the outcome of your life.
sentences.zh: 你手里握着十支飞镖，它们代表将决定你人生结局的十个大胆决定。

sentences.en: But you don't even have a dartboard to aim at.
sentences.zh: 但你连一个靶子都没有。

sentences.en: In other words, you don't even have a chance to hit the board.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你连击中靶子的机会都没有。

sentences.en: You don't know where the board is.
sentences.zh: 你不知道靶子在哪里。

sentences.en: But of course there is a benefit to actually being lost.
sentences.zh: 但当然，迷失本身也有好处。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that you should never feel lost in your life, because when you're lost, you have a decision to make.
sentences.zh: 我不是说你人生中永远不该感到迷失，因为当你迷失时，你有一个决定要做。

sentences.en: You either let entropy drag you into oblivion, which is that your life gets slowly worse and worse over time without you really noticing it until it's so bad.
sentences.zh: 你要么让熵把你拖入虚无，也就是你的人生随着时间慢慢变糟，你几乎察觉不到，直到它糟透了。

sentences.en: It's like your room getting messy.
sentences.zh: 就像你的房间变乱。

sentences.en: You don't clean your room one day, and then shirts appear over here, and then you don't clean it the next.
sentences.zh: 你一天不打扫，衣服开始出现在这边，第二天你又不打扫。

sentences.en: Then you start to notice dust is gathering, and eventually, day after day, it becomes a pigsty.
sentences.zh: 然后你开始注意到灰尘在堆积，最终，日复一日，它变成了一个猪窝。

sentences.en: And it's normal to you.
sentences.zh: 而你对它习以为常。

sentences.en: That's the dangerous part, is that it doesn't just rapidly get dirty.
sentences.zh: 这才是危险的部分，它不会一下子就变得脏乱不堪。

sentences.en: It happens slowly over time in this way where you don't even notice it, and then it's so much harder to get out.
sentences.zh: 它随着时间缓慢发生，慢到你根本注意不到，然后你就更难脱身了。

sentences.en: And that's what's happening.
sentences.zh: 而这正是正在发生的事。

sentences.en: When you feel lost, you have to make the decision to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 当你感到迷茫时，你必须做出决定，把它搞明白。

sentences.en: Experiment with new things until you find that one thing that's worth going all in on.
sentences.zh: 去尝试新事物，直到你找到那件值得你全身心投入的事。

sentences.en: The void is where success is born.
sentences.zh: 虚空，正是成功诞生的地方。

sentences.en: Now.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: A vision is the ultimate outcome that you're aiming for in life.
sentences.zh: 愿景，是你人生瞄准的终极结果。

sentences.en: It is not a vague wish.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个模糊的愿望。

sentences.en: It must be as specific as it can possibly be.
sentences.zh: 它必须尽可能具体。

sentences.en: It must be compelling enough to motivate and guide every action.
sentences.zh: 它必须有足够的吸引力，能够激励并指引你的每一个行动。

sentences.en: Because you're clear about what you want, you can't have a strategy at all.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你不清楚自己想要什么，你根本不可能有战略。

sentences.en: Once you are clear, you can reverse engineer every step in iterate as you go.
sentences.zh: 一旦你清楚了，你就可以倒推每一步，并在前进中不断迭代。

sentences.en: So if you want to become someone who is emotionally resilient or deeply self-aware in financially independent by 35, that's very specific.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想在35岁前成为一个情绪坚韧、深度自省、经济独立的人，这就非常具体。

sentences.en: That allows you to evaluate every daily decision against it.
sentences.zh: 这让你能够用这个标准去衡量每一个日常决策。

sentences.en: Scrolling social media for two hours probably doesn't move you toward that, and without vision, you wouldn't even register that as a problem in your life.
sentences.zh: 刷两小时社交媒体大概不会让你朝那个方向前进，而没有愿景，你甚至不会意识到那是个问题。

sentences.en: As another example, if you want to build a 50,000 follower, audience or newsletter in the personal development space, that generates enough revenue to quit your job in 18 months, again, that is very specific.
sentences.zh: 再举个例子，如果你想在个人成长领域建立一个5万粉丝的受众或 newsletter，并在18个月内产生足够让你辞职的收入，同样，这非常具体。

sentences.en: That is doable.
sentences.zh: 这是可以做到的。

sentences.en: You can actively see whether or not your actions are leading toward that, and then you can course correct when they're not.
sentences.zh: 你可以主动审视自己的行动是否在导向那个目标，如果没有，你就可以及时纠偏。

sentences.en: Or you can educate so that you know what to do and you know what tactics to apply, and you know whether or not the tactics apply to you so you don't get sucked down the distraction rabbit hole on social media of people trying to tell you their business model is better.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以去学习，这样你就知道该做什么，知道该用什么策略，也知道这些策略是否适合你，这样你就不会被社交媒体上那些试图告诉你他们的商业模式更好的人拖进分心的兔子洞。

sentences.en: Every piece of content that you write, every platform choice, and where you choose to grow on social media.
sentences.zh: 你写的每一篇内容，你选择的每一个平台，以及你选择在社交媒体上哪里增长。

sentences.en: Every monetization decision can be evaluated against the intent.
sentences.zh: 每一个变现决策，都可以对照这个意图来评估。

sentences.en: And now, since everyone's talking about building a personal brand these days and I'm with them, I do think it is the future in many ways, especially as a value creator, not necessarily an influencer that contributes to brain rot and ruining people's minds, but someone who explores their curiosity and shares what they learn and provides some form of value.
sentences.zh: 现在，既然所有人都在谈论打造个人品牌，我也认同他们，我确实认为这在很多方面是未来，尤其是作为一个价值创造者，而不是一个助长脑腐、毁人心智的网红，而是一个探索自己的好奇心、分享所学、提供某种价值的人。

sentences.en: I do believe that that is a very good path to go down for people that want to go down.
sentences.zh: 我确实相信，对于想走这条路的人来说，这是一条非常好的路。

sentences.en: It now actually created something pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 我为此做了一个挺酷的东西。

sentences.en: The link is in the description, but all you do is you fill out five questions and this is completely free.
sentences.zh: 链接在简介里，你只需要填五个问题，完全免费。

sentences.en: I built it kind of just for fun, but you fill out five questions and then it researches what's working in the market.
sentences.zh: 我做这个纯粹是为了好玩，你填五个问题，然后它会研究市场上什么在奏效。

sentences.en: And then at the end it spits out a personal brand strategy for you that you resonate with.
sentences.zh: 最后它会为你生成一个与你共鸣的个人品牌策略。

sentences.en: And it builds a board inside of Eden with a swipe file of posts that you can use as inspiration to create your first post, because they are based on what works and what's performing in the market. So it's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 它会在 Eden 里建一个看板，附带一个帖子素材库，你可以用来作为创作第一篇帖子的灵感，因为这些都基于市场上有效、表现好的内容。所以挺酷的。

sentences.en: Try it out.
sentences.zh: 试试看。

sentences.en: And if you're listening to the Spotify version of this video, just go to Eden.
sentences.zh: 如果你在听这个视频的 Spotify 版本，直接去 Eden 就行。

sentences.en: So strategy.
sentences.zh: 那么，战略。

sentences.en: Now the thing here is that vision is very difficult to create just by thinking about it or imagining it.
sentences.zh: 这里的关键是，光靠想或想象，很难创造出愿景。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to think about what you want and actually know whether or not that's what you want.
sentences.zh: 很难去想你想要什么，并且真正知道那是不是你想要的。

sentences.en: So instead, it's easier to start with inverting it, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，反过来，从反面入手会更容易，对吧？

sentences.en: An anti vision or creating a post mortem for your life.
sentences.zh: 一个反愿景，或者为你的人生写一份事后剖析。

sentences.en: And a postmortem is essentially writing out every single thing that went wrong so that you can avoid it.
sentences.zh: 事后剖析本质上就是写下每一件出问题的事，这样你就能避开它们。

sentences.en: So that's step one. That's what I want you to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是第一步。这就是我希望你做的事。

sentences.en: I want you to stop, take out your notes, take out a piece of paper, and just quickly write this down and you can iterate it and add to it over time.
sentences.zh: 我希望你停下来，拿出你的笔记，拿出一张纸，快速把这些写下来，你可以随着时间不断迭代和补充。

sentences.en: First write your anti vision. Just one paragraph.
sentences.zh: 首先写下你的反愿景。就一段话。

sentences.en: Think of exactly what you don't want the outcome of your life to be.
sentences.zh: 想清楚你绝对不希望你的人生结局是什么样子。

sentences.en: The second thing is a post mortem.
sentences.zh: 第二件事是事后复盘。

sentences.en: So reverse engineer why that anti vision would have happened in the first place and what mistakes were made and how to avoid them.
sentences.zh: 倒推一下，这个反愿景最初为什么会发生，犯了哪些错误，以及如何避免它们。

sentences.en: And from there, it's much easier now to think about what your starting vision could be, your MVPs or your minimum viable vision, because it does evolve over time as situations change.
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，思考你的起始愿景、你的最小可行愿景就容易多了，因为随着情况变化，它会不断演化。

sentences.en: So you just need one paragraph, one idea of what your vision is right now so that you have something to improve because you can't improve what doesn't exist.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要一段话，一个关于你当前愿景的想法，这样你就有东西可以改进，因为你无法改进不存在的东西。

sentences.en: So principle number two is research.
sentences.zh: 第二个原则是研究。

sentences.en: And we'll start with a quote from Devin Erickson.
sentences.zh: 我们从 Devin Erickson 的一句话开始。

sentences.en: Worry less about which career skills AI will take over, and more about whether you are training to be and training your kids to be high agency, perceptive, self-motivated people who can navigate an unknowable future with an adaptable mind.
sentences.zh: 少去担心哪些职业技能会被 AI 取代，多去关注你是否在训练自己、训练你的孩子成为高自主性、有洞察力、自我驱动的人，能够用适应性思维去应对不可知的未来。

sentences.en: So in a war, a general sends out spies, studies the terrain, and learns the enemy's habits and tendencies because you need Intel before you act.
sentences.zh: 在战争中，将军会派出间谍，研究地形，了解敌人的习惯和倾向，因为行动之前你需要情报。

sentences.en: The question is, when was the last time you studied yourself?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你上一次研究自己是什么时候？

sentences.en: When was the last time you audited your habits and what kind of life they were compounding into?
sentences.zh: 你上一次审视自己的习惯，以及这些习惯正在把你复利成什么样的生活，是什么时候？

sentences.en: When was the last time you paid attention to how your mind reacts to silly little things that end up clogging your headspace for hours on end, removing you from your path?
sentences.zh: 你上一次留意你的大脑对那些愚蠢小事作何反应，而这些小事最终堵塞你的头脑空间好几个小时、让你偏离轨道，是什么时候？

sentences.en: Most people have zero Intel on how to start a business, how to build a career, what healthy relationships look like, how to stay lean and healthy, or what the mass reprocess looks like.
sentences.zh: 大多数人对于如何创业、如何建立职业生涯、健康的亲密关系是什么样、如何保持精瘦和健康、或者大众再加工过程是什么样，掌握的情报为零。

sentences.en: They get a little spurt of motivation, like for a New Year's resolution, go about it blindly and obviously fail because they didn't engage in research and self-education.
sentences.zh: 他们得到一点动力的小爆发，比如新年决心，然后盲目地去做，显然会失败，因为他们没有进行研究，没有自我教育。

sentences.en: That's not a habit for them.
sentences.zh: 那对他们来说不是一个习惯。

sentences.en: So before you begin improving your life with something like a spirituality practice or anything else, you want to study multiple traditions, read the research on different techniques, talk to people who've done it for years, follow a range of social accounts in that domain, and understand your own psychological patterns and what tends to trigger you.
sentences.zh: 所以在你开始用灵修练习之类的东西改善生活之前，你要去研究多种传统，阅读不同技巧的研究文献，和做了很多年的人聊聊，关注那个领域里一系列社交账号，并理解你自己的心理模式以及什么容易触发你。

sentences.en: You don't just grab the first meditation app that shows up on an Instagram ad, or the first tactic that someone tells you for clearing your mind and being happy all the time that you saw as a tweet or YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 你不是随便抓一个 Instagram 广告里跳出来的冥想 App，或者某个人在一条推文或 YouTube 视频里告诉你的、用来清空大脑和一直快乐的第一个技巧就开始用。

sentences.en: The same thing goes for social media.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体也是一样。

sentences.en: If you're treating this as something that you actually want to do well at, you need a strategy.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这件事当成你真的想做好的一件事，你需要一个策略。

sentences.en: You need to study what other people in the market are doing.
sentences.zh: 你需要研究市场上其他人在做什么。

sentences.en: You need to understand what works, and you need to let that inform your strategy.
sentences.zh: 你需要理解什么有效，并让这些信息来指导你的策略。

sentences.en: You need to use a research tool like Eden or the other ones, and scroll the discover feed and see what's working, and scroll social media and save posts so that you have them ready.
sentences.zh: 你需要使用像 Eden 这样的研究工具或者其他工具，浏览发现页，看看什么在奏效，浏览社交媒体并保存帖子，这样你就有了素材储备。

sentences.en: When it's time to write.
sentences.zh: 等到写作的时候。

sentences.en: You curate lists of creators and you study them.
sentences.zh: 你策划创作者名单，然后研究他们。

sentences.en: You don't just blindly scroll social media, and once you have enough research, you begin to strategize.
sentences.zh: 你不是盲目地刷社交媒体，一旦你有了足够的研究，你就开始制定策略。

sentences.en: How can you wedge yourself into the market by doing what works, but by doing also what is unique.
sentences.zh: 你如何通过做有效的事，同时也做独特的事，把自己楔入市场。

sentences.en: This is the downfall of starving artists, because all they want to do is practice their little art.
sentences.zh: 这就是穷困艺术家的败落之处，因为他们只想练习他们那点小艺术。

sentences.en: But they won't merge it with business.
sentences.zh: 但他们不愿意把它和商业融合。

sentences.en: They won't integrate the two.
sentences.zh: 他们不愿意把二者整合起来。

sentences.en: They think that by simply going about it in a business way, just strips all the humanity and soul from it.
sentences.zh: 他们认为只要用商业的方式去做，就会剥离掉所有的人性和灵魂。

sentences.en: When that's not anywhere close to the case, you're just not thinking again.
sentences.zh: 而事实远非如此，你只是又没有在思考罢了。

sentences.en: You're thinking in black and white.
sentences.zh: 你在用非黑即白的方式思考。

sentences.en: You're letting other people's beliefs and polarizing opinions infect your mind, and you're not questioning them.
sentences.zh: 你让别人的信念和极端观点感染了你的大脑，而且你从不质疑它们。

sentences.en: You're not coming up with your own opinion on the matter.
sentences.zh: 你没有形成自己对这件事的看法。

sentences.en: Because obviously, if your goal is to actually see success and then you go and do something completely different because your beliefs are tainted, then that's not ideal.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，如果你的目标是真正获得成功，结果你却因为信念被污染而去做完全相反的事，那就不理想了。

sentences.en: So if you just want to write as art, then go ahead and do it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你只是想把写作当成艺术，那就去做吧。

sentences.en: But don't expect anyone to give you your attention just because you spent a lot of time writing.
sentences.zh: 但别指望别人会因为你花了很多时间写作就给你注意力。

sentences.en: Because time does not equate to value, it is okay.
sentences.zh: 因为时间不等于价值，这没什么。

sentences.en: It is perfectly okay to treat writing or art as a hobby.
sentences.zh: 把写作或艺术当成爱好完全没问题。

sentences.en: But if you're trying to do this as a form of meaningful work, then it is a business.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想把它作为一种有意义的工作来做，那它就是一门生意。

sentences.en: Now, principle number three is preparation, and this is where you identify your resources, the resources that you specifically have and your gaps.
sentences.zh: 好，原则三是准备，这一步你要识别你的资源，你具体拥有的资源以及你的缺口。

sentences.en: Because you wouldn't just drop into a battlefield without food or logistics or weapons or support.
sentences.zh: 因为你不会在没有食物、后勤、武器或支援的情况下就直接投入战场。

sentences.en: And so once you know what resources you have or the ones that you don't, you can start building reserves so that eventually you can execute on your strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你知道了自己拥有哪些资源、缺少哪些资源，你就可以开始建立储备，以便最终执行你的战略。

sentences.en: The resources that most people need to look for are money, time, knowledge, skills, the location you live, connections, and relationships.
sentences.zh: 大多数人需要寻找的资源是：金钱、时间、知识、技能、你居住的地点、人脉和关系。

sentences.en: All of those things are valid resources.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都算有效资源。

sentences.en: Just because you don't have money doesn't mean that you can't create a strategy to say, start a business because you can still develop skill, you can develop knowledge, and if you're young, you have plenty of time on your hands, right?
sentences.zh: 你没有钱，不代表你无法制定战略去创业，因为你仍然可以发展技能、积累知识，而且如果你年轻，你手里有大把时间，对吧？

sentences.en: The ones who are past the age of 20, 25, 30, when they're very ingrained in their habits and they have bills to pay and all these responsibilities, they don't have much time or money on their hands.
sentences.zh: 那些过了20、25、30岁的人，当他们深陷于自己的习惯，有账单要付、有各种责任要扛，他们手里就没有太多时间或金钱了。

sentences.en: So if you lack those resources and they're very difficult to get, what other resources can you go after?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你缺乏这些资源，而且它们很难获取，那你可以去争取哪些其他资源？

sentences.en: Where can you leverage yourself as an example before attempting some kind of major life change, like quitting a job, or ending a relationship, or starting a new project or venture, you'd probably want to build your financial runway, decrease your expenses, develop the emotional regulation skills you'll need, and line up support systems.
sentences.zh: 在你尝试某种重大人生改变之前——比如辞职、结束一段关系、启动一个新项目或新事业——你最好先建立财务跑道、降低开支、培养你需要的情绪调节能力，并安排好支持系统。

sentences.en: You don't just rush into battle.
sentences.zh: 你不会直接冲进战场。

sentences.en: In other words, you need to hedge against risk because every goal comes with risk.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你需要对冲风险，因为每个目标都伴随着风险。

sentences.en: And as you go deeper and deeper into the hierarchy of goals you're trying to achieve, the risk only gets greater and greater.
sentences.zh: 随着你在目标层级中越走越深，风险只会越来越大。

sentences.en: You may start a business as a one person business, like we talk about with something like an information product or a simple AI product.
sentences.zh: 你可能会以一人企业的形式创业，就像我们聊过的，比如做一个信息产品或者一个简单的AI产品。

sentences.en: But then what's next?
sentences.zh: 但接下来呢？

sentences.en: Are you going to build a team or are you going to expand, or are you going to go into e-commerce?
sentences.zh: 你是要建立团队，还是要扩张，还是要进入电商领域？

sentences.en: What else are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 你还打算做什么？

sentences.en: Or are you going to stick and make it a lifestyle business, which is perfectly valid?
sentences.zh: 还是说你会坚持下去，把它做成一个生活方式生意，这也完全合理。

sentences.en: But if you want a greater return, if you want more money or potentially more freedom or just whatever you want in life, what is your vision, then you're going to have to build the resources so that the risk of doing so doesn't absolutely destroy you.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想要更大的回报，如果你想要更多钱、或者更多自由、或者任何你人生中想要的东西——你的愿景是什么——那你就必须积累资源，这样去追求它的风险才不会彻底摧毁你。

sentences.en: So if you don't have many resources, then it probably wouldn't make sense to start crypto trading or start stock trading or day trading, because you're just going to lose all your money.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你没有太多资源，那去搞加密货币交易、股票交易或者日内交易可能就不太合理，因为你只会亏光所有钱。

sentences.en: You're gambling at that point, and that's not a strategy.
sentences.zh: 到那个地步你就是在赌博，那不是战略。

sentences.en: You are much better off starting smaller so that you can acquire resources.
sentences.zh: 你从更小的事情开始要好得多，这样你才能获取资源。

sentences.en: That is the beginning of your strategy is how do I do something that allows me to get the resources I need to do what I eventually want to do?
sentences.zh: 你战略的起点就是：我如何做一些事，让我能获得我最终想做那件事所需的资源？

sentences.en: So the way that I went about that is social media.
sentences.zh: 我走这条路的方式是社交媒体。

sentences.en: I knew that it was free to access.
sentences.zh: 我知道它是免费获取的。

sentences.en: I didn't need any money to start the business.
sentences.zh: 我创业不需要任何钱。

sentences.en: I didn't need any money to create an info product.
sentences.zh: 我创建信息产品不需要任何钱。

sentences.en: I didn't need any money to write a book.
sentences.zh: 我写书不需要任何钱。

sentences.en: And then that allowed me to acquire the resource of money so that I could invest into a bigger business that I wanted to build, which is in the software business.
sentences.zh: 然后这让我获得了金钱这个资源，我就能把它投入到我想建立的更大的事业里，也就是软件业务。

sentences.en: And eventually, soon Sonder, the new tropic business.
sentences.zh: 很快，Sonder 这个新的 tropic 业务也会推出。

sentences.en: So if you have these high and mighty dreams of doing something massive, right, which I think is a very worthwhile thing to do and to think about, but it's not feasible for you right now.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有那些宏大高远的梦想，想做点大事——我觉得这非常值得去做、去思考——但它现在对你来说还不现实。

sentences.en: What are you doing about it?
sentences.zh: 那你正在为此做什么？

sentences.en: Just because you can't start the business you want to start now, doesn't mean you can't start another form of a business that allows you to start that business.
sentences.zh: 你现在不能开始你想做的那个事业，不代表你不能开始另一种形式的事业，让你最终能开始那个事业。

sentences.en: Otherwise, you're never going to be able to start the one you want to start.
sentences.zh: 否则，你永远都没法开始你真正想做的那个。

sentences.en: Now.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Speaking specifically to young people, you have so much time on your hands.
sentences.zh: 专门对年轻人说几句：你手里有大把时间。

sentences.en: You are in one of the greatest positions you can possibly be right now at this point in your life.
sentences.zh: 你正处在人生这个阶段能拥有的最有利的位置之一。

sentences.en: And if you have these high and mighty dreams, in my opinion, the best thing you can do is just hedge against risk as much as you can so that you can take risk and have nothing to lose.
sentences.zh: 如果你有那些宏大高远的梦想，在我看来，你能做的最好的事就是尽可能对冲风险，这样你才能去冒险，而且没什么可失去的。

sentences.en: What that means is selling everything you own.
sentences.zh: 这意味着卖掉你拥有的一切。

sentences.en: Living in a depression apartment as Devin calls it, a.k.a an apartment that costs nothing.
sentences.zh: 住进 Devin 所说的"抑郁公寓"，也就是那种几乎不花钱的公寓。

sentences.en: You just have no standard of living for your young years, and you cut all your expenses so that everything you have can go into the thing that you're building because you have the resource of time, but you don't have the resource of money.
sentences.zh: 在你年轻的时候，干脆不要什么生活标准，砍掉所有开支，让你拥有的一切都能投入到你正在构建的事情里，因为你拥有时间这个资源，但你没有金钱这个资源。

sentences.en: So you need to pull all of your reserves in and put it toward generating the resource of money.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要把所有储备都集中起来，投入到产生金钱这个资源上。

sentences.en: Now, principle number four of strategic thinking is focus specifically concentration of force.
sentences.zh: 好，战略思维的第四条原则是聚焦，具体来说是力量集中。

sentences.en: So a quote from Greg McCown from the book essentialism.
sentences.zh: 引用 Greg McKeown 在《精要主义》这本书里的一句话。

sentences.en: Is there a point at which doing more does not produce more?
sentences.zh: 是否存在一个临界点，做得更多并不会产出更多？

sentences.en: Is there a point at which doing less but thinking more will actually produce better outcomes?
sentences.zh: 是否存在一个临界点，做得更少但思考更多，反而会带来更好的结果？

sentences.en: So focus or concentration of force is the military principle of focusing all of your resources at the decisive point, rather than spreading thin.
sentences.zh: 所以聚焦或者说力量集中，是一个军事原则，指把所有资源集中在决定性的一点上，而不是分散摊薄。

sentences.en: The best example of this is France in 1940, where the French had more tanks and troops than the Germans, and they had far more raw resources, but they distributed their armor or tanks evenly across the entire front.
sentences.zh: 最好的例子是 1940 年的法国，当时法军的坦克和兵力都比德军多，原始资源也远超德军，但他们把装甲部队或者说坦克均匀地分布在整个前线上。

sentences.en: So every sector had a few tanks.
sentences.zh: 所以每个防区只有几辆坦克。

sentences.en: The Germans took every panzer they had and drove them through a single point, which the French thought was impassable, so they barely defended it.
sentences.zh: 德军则把他们所有的装甲车集中起来，从一个单点突破，而法军认为那个地方无法通行，所以几乎没设防。

sentences.en: Focus is about where you put what you have, and in life you only have so much of it at any given time.
sentences.zh: 聚焦是关于你把拥有的东西放在哪里，而在人生中，你在任何特定时刻拥有的东西都是有限的。

sentences.en: Most people try to change their life and place 10% of their attention into diet, sleep, exercise, meditation, relationships, their side hustle, and more.
sentences.zh: 大多数人试图改变生活时，会把 10% 的注意力放在饮食、睡眠、锻炼、冥想、人际关系、副业等等上面。

sentences.en: When they would get better at all of them faster if they focused on the single bottleneck holding them back the most.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们聚焦在阻碍自己最大的那个单一瓶颈上，反而能在所有这些方面都更快地变好。

sentences.en: I don't think people understand that enough.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们对此理解得远远不够。

sentences.en: That focus does not decrease your progress in all areas.
sentences.zh: 聚焦并不会减缓你在其他领域的进展。

sentences.en: It increases them in all areas.
sentences.zh: 它会加速你在所有领域的进展。

sentences.en: By focusing on one thing, you increase every other area, and for most people, the single bottleneck is money because money buys anything.
sentences.zh: 通过聚焦一件事，你提升了其他每一个领域，而对大多数人来说，那个单一瓶颈就是钱，因为钱能买到任何东西。

sentences.en: So if you focus solely on solving your financial struggle first, then that frees up more resources to put towards other areas of your life, like diet.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你先专注于解决财务困境，那就能释放出更多资源投入到生活的其他方面，比如饮食。

sentences.en: You can afford higher quality food.
sentences.zh: 你能买得起更高质量的食物。

sentences.en: When you have more money, you're in a less stressful state.
sentences.zh: 当你有更多钱时，你处在一个压力更小的状态里。

sentences.en: You can think more creatively.
sentences.zh: 你能更有创造力地思考。

sentences.en: It benefits your creative work and spirituality.
sentences.zh: 这对你的创造性工作和精神世界都有好处。

sentences.en: And with those three things a clear mind and a better diet and more energy and potentially more time to go and exercise that benefits your relationships in.
sentences.zh: 有了这三样东西——清晰的头脑、更好的饮食、更多的精力，以及可能更多的时间去锻炼——你的人际关系也会受益。

sentences.en: The same applies to business.
sentences.zh: 商业上同理。

sentences.en: On something like social media, there is more to growth than just content, so cross posting to all platforms takes away time you could be spending building connections with people that will help you grow.
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体这类事情上，增长远不止内容本身，所以跨平台分发会挤占你本该用来建立人脉的时间，而那些人脉能帮你成长。

sentences.en: You'd gain more followers by focusing on one platform first, which can then be used as leverage to grow on the other platforms faster than you would have in the same amount of time, spreading your force across all platforms.
sentences.zh: 先专注一个平台，你会涨更多粉丝，然后以此为杠杆，在同样时间内，比你把力量分散到所有平台能更快地带动其他平台的增长。

sentences.en: One tangible example of that is that I chose Twitter or X as my first platform, and I solely focused on that.
sentences.zh: 一个具体的例子是，我选了 Twitter 或者说 X 作为我的第一个平台，并且只专注那里。

sentences.en: I built connections on that platform, and I still know and talk to those connections today.
sentences.zh: 我在那个平台建立了人脉，至今我仍然认识他们、和他们有交流。

sentences.en: But when I had somewhat of a large following on Twitter, when I decided I wanted to deploy my strategy on Instagram and grow there, I found people with a large following on Instagram and said, hey, I have a large following on X, do you want to help each other grow by sharing each other's content on either platform?
sentences.zh: 但当我在 Twitter 上有了相当规模的关注者之后，我决定把策略部署到 Instagram 并在那里增长，我找到在 Instagram 上有大量关注者的人，跟他们说，嘿，我在 X 上有大量关注者，要不要我们互相分享内容，帮对方在两个平台上增长？

sentences.en: And that alone allowed me to grow on Instagram so much faster than anyone else just starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 光凭这一点，我在 Instagram 上的增长速度就远超那些从零开始的人。

sentences.en: This is something we teach in week four of the Creator Bootcamp.
sentences.zh: 这是我们 Creator Bootcamp 第四周教的内容。

sentences.en: Now, principle number five of strategic thinking is just execute or execution.
sentences.zh: 好，战略思维的第五条原则就是：执行，纯粹的执行。

sentences.en: And from Alex Hermosa, strategy is how you choose to allocate your limited resources against unlimited options.
sentences.zh: 引用 Alex Hermosa 的话：战略，就是你如何选择把有限的资源分配到无限的选择上。

sentences.en: Proper execution of strategy is the continuous act of jumping between macro vision and micro daily action, ensuring that the decisions you make have aim and intention.
sentences.zh: 战略的正确执行，是在宏观愿景和微观日常行动之间持续跳跃，确保你做的每一个决定都有方向和意图。

sentences.en: This is the core of what strategy is doing.
sentences.zh: 这才是战略的核心。

sentences.en: The opposite of what 99% of people do, because most people do not think outside of their conditioning, assigned goals or repetitive routines.
sentences.zh: 这和 99% 的人所做的截然相反，因为大多数人不会跳出自己的条件反射、被指派的目标或重复的日常去思考。

sentences.en: But how do you actually execute effectively?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么才能真正有效地执行？

sentences.en: This is where everything starts to come together.
sentences.zh: 从这里开始，一切开始汇聚成形。

sentences.en: First, you practice holding your vision in the back of your mind.
sentences.zh: 第一，练习把愿景放在你脑海深处。

sentences.en: Write it down somewhere and look at it every morning.
sentences.zh: 把它写下来，每天早上看一眼。

sentences.en: It must become a part of who you are through repeat exposure.
sentences.zh: 它必须通过反复接触，成为你身份的一部分。

sentences.en: Second, take note of what you learn from studying your opponents or yourself.
sentences.zh: 第二，记下你研究对手或研究自己时学到的东西。

sentences.en: Meditate on it. Contemplate it.
sentences.zh: 去冥想它。去沉思它。

sentences.en: Let it marinate in your mind so that it can start to make connections.
sentences.zh: 让它在你的脑海里浸泡，这样它才能开始产生连接。

sentences.en: Third, identify the primary resource that you can leverage for young people.
sentences.zh: 第三，识别出你可以利用的首要资源。对年轻人来说——

sentences.en: It's time and freedom.
sentences.zh: 是时间和自由。

sentences.en: Most likely.
sentences.zh: 大概率是这样。

sentences.en: For some, its capital.
sentences.zh: 对一些人来说，是资本。

sentences.en: For others, it's an internet audience.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人，是互联网受众。

sentences.en: For more, it's a weird set of interests and knowledge.
sentences.zh: 对更多人来说，是一套奇怪的兴趣和知识组合。

sentences.en: And yes, for many it's AI, but not from the low level sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，对很多人来说，是 AI，但不是从低层次的意义上。

sentences.en: AI gives high agency people the ability to do so much more, and it gives low agency people a reason to play victim and complain.
sentences.zh: AI 让高自主性的人有能力做到多得多的事情，也让低自主性的人有了扮演受害者、不停抱怨的理由。

sentences.en: But the trap for the high agency person is that now they have unlimited options.
sentences.zh: 但高自主性的人面临的陷阱是，现在他们有了无限的选择。

sentences.en: They can do anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么都能做。

sentences.en: So concentration of force strategic thinking is even more important than ever because you can do anything with AI, but that doesn't mean you're going to get anywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以，集中力量进行战略思考，现在比以往任何时候都更重要——因为有了 AI，你什么都能做，但这并不意味着你能做成任何事。

sentences.en: And fourth, choose your concentration of force play.
sentences.zh: 第四，选择你的集中力量打法。

sentences.en: Where is the single highest leverage point, the one that would unlock progress in more than one domain?
sentences.zh: 那个唯一的、最高的杠杆点在哪里？就是那个能在不止一个领域打开局面的点。

sentences.en: The thing that makes everything else easier.
sentences.zh: 那个让其他一切都变得更容易的东西。

sentences.en: And from there we have a soft plan.
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，我们有一个软性的计划。

sentences.en: But it needs to be crystal clear.
sentences.zh: 但它必须极其清晰。

sentences.en: We have to reverse engineer our vision down into a hierarchy of goals that allows us to gain perspective and clarity on our daily actions.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把愿景倒推，拆解成一个目标层级，让我们能看清每天的日常行动，获得视角和清晰度。

sentences.en: They can't be so far away from each other.
sentences.zh: 它们之间不能离得太远。

sentences.en: You have to see how your daily actions slowly contribute to your vision, because in many cases, they're not going to directly contribute to it.
sentences.zh: 你必须看到你的日常行动是如何一步步为你的愿景做出贡献的，因为在很多情况下，它们并不会直接贡献。

sentences.en: You're going to take a daily action, and you're not going to be able to see how it actually is creating your vision.
sentences.zh: 你会采取一个日常行动，然后你无法直接看到它到底是怎么创造你的愿景的。

sentences.en: That's why you have to break it down and see the entire system.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你必须把它拆解开来，看到整个系统。

sentences.en: So take your vision and then work backward to one your goals, 90 day objectives, weekly priorities, and daily habits.
sentences.zh: 所以，拿出你的愿景，然后往回推：到你的年度目标、90天目标、每周优先事项，再到每日习惯。

sentences.en: Every step should trace back to the intent or vision.
sentences.zh: 每一步都应该能追溯到那个意图或愿景。

sentences.en: If it doesn't set it aside, that is your sign to take the piece of paper that you took out earlier and to write this down with everything else.
sentences.zh: 如果追溯不到，就把它放到一边——这就是一个信号，让你拿出之前那张纸，把这个和其他所有东西一起写下来。

sentences.en: Now, principle number six is adapt or adaptability.
sentences.zh: 现在，第六个原则是适应，或者说适应性。

sentences.en: And a quote for me accept Mihai.
sentences.zh: 有一句话我很认同，来自 Mihai。

sentences.en: It is not possible to experience a feeling of control unless one is willing to give up the safety of protective routines only when a doubtful outcome is at stake and one is able to influence that outcome, can a person really know whether she is in control.
sentences.zh: 一个人不可能体验到掌控感，除非她愿意放弃那些保护性惯例带来的安全感。只有当结果不确定、成败悬而未决，而她又能影响那个结果时，一个人才真正知道自己是否在掌控之中。

sentences.en: What that means is that a rigid strategy or routine is a losing strategy or routine, especially in today's world where the rate of change is extreme.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，一个僵化的策略或惯例，就是一个注定失败的东西，尤其是在当今这个变化速度极快的世界里。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: During the industrial age and up until now, not too much change.
sentences.zh: 在工业时代，一直到不久前，变化都不算大。

sentences.en: That's why it's so deeply ingrained to go to school, get a job, retire at 65 because the societal system was built up according to that paradigm, with the goal.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么“上学、找工作、65岁退休”这件事如此根深蒂固，因为整个社会系统就是按照那个范式、那个目标建立起来的。

sentences.en: But now with AI and disruption and all of this stuff, everything is changing every 3 to 6 months and the rate of change will only increase.
sentences.zh: 但现在，有了 AI、颠覆和所有这些，每3到6个月一切都在变，而且变化的速度只会越来越快。

sentences.en: And it's going to filter out so many people who get stuck with a rigid strategy and aren't able to adapt.
sentences.zh: 这会淘汰掉非常多的人——那些固守僵化策略、无法适应的人。

sentences.en: So in my eyes, the future belongs to the true strategists at this higher level of thinking that will dive into more in the next video.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，未来属于真正的战略家，属于这种更高层次的思考者，我们会在下一个视频里深入探讨。

sentences.en: Because masters can adapt on the fly, because they have the universal principles that they can apply to all domains, they don't necessarily need to relearn everything.
sentences.zh: 因为大师能够临场应变，他们掌握了可以应用到所有领域的通用原则，他们不一定需要从头学起。

sentences.en: They don't need to upskill or reskill or reeducate because they can do that extremely fast on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要去提升技能、重新学技能或重新受教育，因为他们自己就能极快地做到这些。

sentences.en: So your job is to respond to what's actually happening then and there on the battlefield, not your mental fabrications of worst case scenarios or your fantasies that are not yet real.
sentences.zh: 所以你的任务是：回应战场上此时此刻实际发生的事情，而不是你脑子里臆想的最坏情况，或者那些尚未成真的幻想。

sentences.en: So if you committed to a morning routine as an example, but your job schedule changed, you don't just abandon the routine.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果你坚持一个晨间惯例，但你的工作时间表变了，你不要直接放弃那个惯例。

sentences.en: That's what most people do.
sentences.zh: 那是大多数人会做的事。

sentences.en: Don't do what most people do.
sentences.zh: 不要做大多数人做的事。

sentences.en: The vision and intent of your strategy doesn't change, which is becoming, let's say, more disciplined and grounded.
sentences.zh: 你策略中的愿景和意图不会变——比如说，那个意图是变得更自律、更沉稳。

sentences.en: That's why you created a morning routine.
sentences.zh: 这就是你当初创建晨间惯例的原因。

sentences.en: But the tactics do.
sentences.zh: 但具体战术会变。

sentences.en: If a particular meditation or business strategy stops working after six months, then you need to change.
sentences.zh: 如果某个冥想方式或商业策略用了六个月后不再有效，那你就需要改变。

sentences.en: You need to experiment and try something new.
sentences.zh: 你需要去实验，去尝试新东西。

sentences.en: You need to be in the constant state of experimentation.
sentences.zh: 你需要一直处于实验状态。

sentences.en: And that's just the principle that systems fall apart over time.
sentences.zh: 这背后的原理就是：系统会随着时间瓦解。

sentences.en: You should expect that.
sentences.zh: 你应该预料到这一点。

sentences.en: Think of the notion system that you built out six months ago and don't use now, or the cloud skill you downloaded and don't use anymore.
sentences.zh: 想想你六个月前搭好的 Notion 系统现在不用了，或者你下载的 Claude 技能现在也不用了。

sentences.en: You have to be skilled enough to know when something isn't working.
sentences.zh: 你必须足够敏锐，能判断出什么东西不管用了。

sentences.en: The same is true with social media.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体也是一样。

sentences.en: I have people come to me all the time and it's like, Dan, I posted this and it was supposed to work according to all of these things that I learned, but it didn't work. What do I do?
sentences.zh: 总有人来找我说，Dan，我发了这个，按我学的所有东西它应该有效，但没效果，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: You adapt, you experiment, you keep trying.
sentences.zh: 你去适应，去实验，继续尝试。

sentences.en: This isn't a job.
sentences.zh: 这不是一份工作。

sentences.en: You don't just study and train a repeatable set of tasks.
sentences.zh: 你不是只学一套可重复的任务然后训练。

sentences.en: You have to have the entrepreneurial mind, the creative mind.
sentences.zh: 你必须有创业者的思维，创造者的思维。

sentences.en: You have to be in this constant state of taking in what's going on and interpreting it and then outputting it, and then slowly getting better at that entire process over time.
sentences.zh: 你必须持续吸收正在发生的事，解读它，然后输出，再随着时间慢慢让这整个过程变得更好。

sentences.en: Now, the way you actually practice this is review, reflection and prediction.
sentences.zh: 那么，实际练习这个的方法就是：回顾、反思和预测。

sentences.en: You need to schedule this weekly.
sentences.zh: 你需要每周安排时间做这件事。

sentences.en: You need to review your week, see if you're on track, reflect on your progress and predict where you're heading.
sentences.zh: 你需要回顾你的一周，看看你是否在轨道上，反思你的进展，预测你正走向哪里。

sentences.en: And this doesn't need to be in any fancy template or thing that you download.
sentences.zh: 这不需要什么花哨的模板或者你下载的东西。

sentences.en: This is like just keep a piece of paper by your computer.
sentences.zh: 就像是在电脑旁边放一张纸就行。

sentences.en: I have this little tiny notebook where I just jot things down because I understand that if I try to keep up with a note taking system, I don't keep up with it.
sentences.zh: 我有个很小的笔记本，我就随手记东西，因为我明白，如果我试图维护一个笔记系统，我根本维护不下去。

sentences.en: That's not how your mind works.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑不是那样工作的。

sentences.en: It kind of has to be messy.
sentences.zh: 它就得有点乱。

sentences.en: You have to embrace just putting an idea down and letting it get lost.
sentences.zh: 你得接受把一个想法写下来，然后让它丢失。

sentences.en: And if it's important, you will remember it.
sentences.zh: 如果它重要，你会记住的。

sentences.en: That's the library feature of even.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Even 的图书馆功能。

sentences.en: You just drop ideas in and we auto tag auto categorize everything for you, but you don't even need that.
sentences.zh: 你只管把想法丢进去，我们自动为你打标签、自动分类，但你甚至不需要那个。

sentences.en: You can use Apple Notes, you can use the notebook, you can use anything.
sentences.zh: 你可以用 Apple Notes，可以用笔记本，可以用任何东西。

sentences.en: Just get in the habit of writing things down.
sentences.zh: 只要养成把东西写下来的习惯。

sentences.en: Now the final principle, number seven the principle of all principles of strategic thinking is the study of principles.
sentences.zh: 最后一个原则，第七个，战略思维的原则中的原则，就是研究原则本身。

sentences.en: Now with this section, I encourage you to adopt the belief that everything is a skill.
sentences.zh: 在这一部分，我鼓励你接受一个信念：一切都是技能。

sentences.en: Everything is a field of study that you can stack, experience in and get better at money, mindset, beliefs, relationships, business, social media.
sentences.zh: 一切都是一个你可以积累经验、不断精进的研究领域——金钱、心态、信念、关系、商业、社交媒体。

sentences.en: Everything that you think is luck is not luck.
sentences.zh: 所有你以为是运气的东西，都不是运气。

sentences.en: It's skill.
sentences.zh: 是技能。

sentences.en: It's only luck because you're gambling and you don't have strategy.
sentences.zh: 它之所以是运气，只是因为你在赌博，你没有战略。

sentences.en: And strategy itself is a field of study with principles that hold across domains.
sentences.zh: 而战略本身就是一个研究领域，其中的原则可以跨领域成立。

sentences.en: The more you study strategy and its principles, the better you become at applying them to your own life situation.
sentences.zh: 你越研究战略及其原理，就越擅长把它们应用到自己的人生处境里。

sentences.en: It is a lifelong, ongoing practice.
sentences.zh: 这是一项终身的、持续的修炼。

sentences.en: So read sunset, read about cognitive biases.
sentences.zh: 所以去读《孙子兵法》，去读认知偏误。

sentences.en: Study how habits form.
sentences.zh: 去研究习惯是怎么形成的。

sentences.en: Learn the principles of negotiation.
sentences.zh: 去学谈判的原理。

sentences.en: Study why content goes viral.
sentences.zh: 去研究内容为什么会病毒式传播。

sentences.en: Study how attention economics works.
sentences.zh: 去研究注意力经济学是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: You don't just copy what other creators do.
sentences.zh: 你不是去抄其他创作者的做法。

sentences.en: You study the principles so you can come up with your own moves.
sentences.zh: 你研究原理，是为了能创造出自己的招式。

sentences.en: That is essentially what originality is.
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是原创性的真正含义。

sentences.en: Because nothing is original, nothing is authentic.
sentences.zh: 因为没有什么是完全原创的，没有什么是绝对真实的。

sentences.en: It honestly peeves me when people, like people get in little arguments on social media of like, oh, you copied my idea and you copied my idea, but you're just looking through the lens of specificity, right? Did they copy your niche?
sentences.zh: 说实话，我很烦社交媒体上那些小争论，比如“你抄了我的创意”“你抄了我的创意”，但你只是透过具体性的镜头在看问题，对吧？他们抄了你的细分领域吗？

sentences.en: You guys write about the same topics?
sentences.zh: 你们写的是同一个话题吗？

sentences.en: Did they copy how you walk?
sentences.zh: 他们抄了你走路的方式吗？

sentences.en: You guys both walk.
sentences.zh: 你们俩都会走路。

sentences.en: You're both human.
sentences.zh: 你们俩都是人。

sentences.en: You both speak the English language.
sentences.zh: 你们俩都说英语。

sentences.en: Did you come up with that all on your own?
sentences.zh: 这些都是你自己凭空想出来的吗？

sentences.en: Did you come up with any of the words that you speak on a daily basis?
sentences.zh: 你每天说的那些词，有哪个是你自己发明的？

sentences.en: Did you create the clothes that you where have you actually audited the beliefs in your head?
sentences.zh: 你穿的衣服是你自己做的吗？你真的审视过自己脑子里的那些信念吗？

sentences.en: How original and authentic are you?
sentences.zh: 你到底有多原创、多真实？

sentences.en: Actually, why do you treat this as some form of high value that you can stand on to virtue, signal to other people when you'd get much better results in life, when you actually leaned in to what nature and authenticity is.
sentences.zh: 说真的，你为什么把这当成某种高价值标签，站在上面向别人炫耀美德，而实际上，当你真正去拥抱自然和真实性的本质时，你的人生会得到好得多的结果。

sentences.en: Now, I'm not saying that plagiarism is good by any means, but I am saying that people take it way too seriously and that people are allowed to have similar ideas.
sentences.zh: 我不是说抄袭是好事，绝对不是，但我是说，人们对这件事太较真了，而且人是可以拥有相似想法的。

sentences.en: They're allowed to post similar ideas under their brand because they resonate with it.
sentences.zh: 他们可以在自己的品牌下发相似的想法，因为他们跟这些想法有共鸣。

sentences.en: But yeah, if it's a direct rip, then yeah, credit the person.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，如果是直接照搬，那就注明出处。

sentences.en: But if it's just an inspired idea.
sentences.zh: 但如果只是一个受启发的想法——

sentences.en: Welcome to how the world works.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到这个世界的运作方式。

sentences.en: Now, beyond that, I believe that the best way to study true principles is to study reality itself, because strategy is the application of reality's principles to human goals.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我相信研究真正原理的最好方式，就是研究现实本身，因为战略就是把现实的原理应用到人类目标上。

sentences.en: So I want to leave you with many different things that you can go down a rabbit hole afterwards.
sentences.zh: 所以我想给你留下很多不同的东西，让你之后可以顺着这些方向深挖下去。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you a long list, and I want you to pick one, and I want you to go and read that thing or buy the book or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 我会给你一个很长的清单，我要你从中挑一个，然后去读那本书，或者去买那本书，不管它是什么。

sentences.en: Just read it and I'll break these up into categories.
sentences.zh: 去读就行，我会把这些分成几个类别。

sentences.en: The first category is just formal systems.
sentences.zh: 第一个类别是形式系统。

sentences.en: The first is cybernetics, the study of feedback loops, control and self-regulation in any system, mechanical, biological or social.
sentences.zh: 第一个是控制论，研究任何系统——机械的、生物的或社会的——中的反馈回路、控制和自我调节。

sentences.en: So go down a rabbit hole with AI or Google about cybernetics systems theory, which is the study of holes, interconnections, stocks and flows, emergence and leverage points.
sentences.zh: 所以去跟 AI 或 Google 深挖一下控制论系统理论，它研究的是整体、互联、存量与流量、涌现以及杠杆点。

sentences.en: Go and buy a book on systems thinking.
sentences.zh: 去买一本系统思考的书。

sentences.en: Third is thermodynamics, especially the second law, because entropy always increases.
sentences.zh: 第三是热力学，尤其是第二定律，因为熵总是在增加。

sentences.en: Every ordered system requires energy input to resist decay.
sentences.zh: 每一个有序系统都需要能量输入来抵抗衰败。

sentences.en: Your habits and routines will fall apart.
sentences.zh: 你的习惯和日常会崩塌。
